4 MapSketch include sketch showing the t: The total area of operations spans a 4.0-mile radius centered at Intracoastal Waterway Mile Marker 245. The primary incident site is at the confluence of the Intracoastal Waterway and Cypress Bayou. A punctured double-hulled barge is discharging Heavy Fuel Oil (HFO 380) at approximately 30 gallons per minute within a 300-yard containment zone, and 1.5 miles of shoreline along the eastern bank of Cypress Bayou is impacted. Threatened areas include the Grand Cypress Mangrove Sanctuary 2.0 miles South-Southeast and Delta Commercial Oyster Leases 3.5 miles down-river. US Coast Guard Aviation Unit 65 observed a 2.0-mile-long by 100-yard-wide surface slick moving with the ebb tide and heavy sheen along the shoreline. The oil plume is moving South-Southeast at 1.8 knots; winds are from the Northwest at 12 knots.
5 Situation Summary and Health and Safet: At 13:50, a tugboat towing two loaded asphalt barges collided with an anchored commercial tanker, rupturing Cargo Tank #2 starboard. Hazards include hydrogen sulfide accumulation, petroleum hydrocarbon inhalation, dermal irritation, slips and falls on oily decks and muddy banks, heat exhaustion in humid 91°F conditions, and drowning during vessel transfers. Establish a 1,000-foot Maritime Safety Zone. Require Level C PPE, half-mask organic vapor respirators, and PFDs for over-water personnel. Maintain continuous multi-gas monitoring near the tank, mandatory work-rest and hydration cycles, and a vessel-based decontamination station at the Cold Zone boundary.
7 Current and Planned Objectives: Complete primary deflection boom deployment across the mouth of Cypress Bayou by 16:30; secure mechanical patching or lightering of Cargo Tank #2 by 18:00; deploy skimming vessels to recover free-floating product before nightfall at 19:30; and establish a full Joint Information Center by 20:00.
ActionsRow1: Coast Guard Station Cypress Bend dispatched Sector Patrol Craft and issued a Notice to Mariners closing the waterway.
ActionsRow2: Captain M. Thorne established Incident Command and deployed first-responder skimmer boats.
ActionsRow3: Port Authority Hazmat Teams completed initial safety sweeps and confirmed no structural fire threats.
ActionsRow4: Marine salvage engineers boarded the barge to inspect damage and prepare transfer pumps.
ActionsRow5: Deploy 2,000 feet of hard boom across the mangrove inlet.
ActionsRow6: Initiate lightering operations to pump fuel out of the damaged tank.
ActionsRow7: Deploy an evening drone overflight to track thermal slick drift patterns.
